what_it_does: Lovable is a browser-based AI product builder for generating and shipping full-stack web applications. Its editor, agent, preview, hosting, and collaboration surfaces are presented as one managed product.
how_it_works: undocumented
scoped_clone_reason: The product identity is context, not a scoped Action Model capability.

what_it_does: Every project lives in a workspace that holds projects, members, billing, and settings. Users can belong to and switch among multiple workspaces.
how_it_works: Workspace is the tenancy and billing container; project access is layered on top.
scoped_clone_reason: A tenant/workspace boundary is needed for client projects, though Lovable’s broad collaboration model is not.

what_it_does: Lovable projects move from editable drafts to published applications. The editor marks the currently live version as Published and supports returning to the latest project state.
how_it_works: Project state is represented by project settings, versions, and publication controls.
scoped_clone_reason: Scoped clone needs a clear draft-to-live lifecycle.

what_it_does: Users describe an application, feature, bug, or change in natural language. Lovable turns the request into edits to the project rather than requiring hand-written code for every change.
how_it_works: Prompt enters the chat panel and is routed to Build or Plan mode.
scoped_clone_reason: Chat-driven constrained code generation is the core 80%-value set in the teardown.

what_it_does: Lovable can use Figma designs as input through a Figma plugin, Figma MCP, or uploaded .fig files. It extracts design variables, colors, typography, and frame structure to reproduce the visual system.
how_it_works: Figma integration parses design artifacts and passes structured design context to the builder.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful for design-led projects but outside the minimum dashboard builder.

what_it_does: Lovable documents GitHub and GitLab export/sync but does not document starting a Lovable project from an existing GitHub repository. Existing-code import is therefore a documented boundary rather than a supported path.
how_it_works: Git integration creates/links a repository from a Lovable project; no documented reverse bootstrap.
scoped_clone_reason: The client needs generated projects, not arbitrary legacy-repository ingestion.

what_it_does: Users can reference project files with @, attach connectors, and reference other projects in the same workspace. Referenced material becomes context for a request.
how_it_works: The chat composer exposes an @ picker and cross-project reads respect workspace permissions.
scoped_clone_reason: Helpful context retrieval; constrained schemas reduce the need for broad references.

what_it_does: Chat accepts images, PDFs, Office documents, audio, and .fig files as context. Images can be zoomed, panned, and annotated before sending.
how_it_works: Attachments are uploaded to the chat message, with documented per-file and per-message limits.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful for briefs and screenshots, but not required for the first scoped build loop.

what_it_does: Users can request focused changes to an existing project instead of regenerating the whole app. Plan sections can also be revised independently before approval.
how_it_works: Build edits the current project; Plan highlighting targets one section for a word-level revision.
scoped_clone_reason: The scoped product must preserve iterative edits against one fixed app shape.

what_it_does: Lovable outputs standard Vite + React projects that can include frontend, backend integrations, and deployment configuration. Generated applications remain editable in the Lovable project.
how_it_works: Build mode modifies project files and backend configuration through agent actions.
scoped_clone_reason: Generated app output is the product’s central artifact.

what_it_does: Paid users can view and edit the full code repository backing a project directly in the Lovable editor. Code mode also provides file references and codebase download paths.
how_it_works: The editor exposes the project file tree and code view alongside the visual preview.
scoped_clone_reason: Code access is valuable, but chat-only constrained generation captures the first release’s value.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud projects can create and evolve database tables and relationships from natural-language requests. The schema is part of the managed backend rather than merely frontend mock data.
how_it_works: Cloud prompts create schema objects and migrations in the project backend.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model owns the database schema and policies; arbitrary schema generation is intentionally removed.

what_it_does: Lovable generates editable React components and UI structure as source code. Its visual-editing system associates rendered elements with stable source-level identities.
how_it_works: A compiler/Vite transformation tags JSX components so preview selection can resolve back to source.
scoped_clone_reason: Component generation remains useful, but DOM-to-source visual mapping can be skipped in v1.

what_it_does: Build requests expose changed files and summaries, while Plan mode shows word-level revisions to a plan. Users can inspect changes before accepting or reverting them.
how_it_works: Details view has Timeline and Changes tabs; Plan view has Show changes and Edit plan toggles.
scoped_clone_reason: Diff visibility is a high-value safety affordance for generated code.

what_it_does: Each version is associated with the originating chat message, and users can jump from history to that message. Activity cards and details show the work that produced a change.
how_it_works: Version entries retain message links and history can open the originating conversation.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful auditability, but not required for the narrow build loop.

what_it_does: Lovable generates application layouts and visual styling from prompts. Its design guidance and templates provide starting points for production-ready visual output.
how_it_works: Build mode emits frontend source and styles; design guidance supplies prompt-level constraints.
scoped_clone_reason: The scoped clone still needs coherent screens from constrained prompts.

what_it_does: Lovable supports reusable design systems and workspace/project visual guidance for colors, typography, spacing, and component conventions. Themes make brand standards reusable across projects.
how_it_works: Design-system and knowledge settings are fed into generation and visual editing context.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model owns one design system; this is simpler than Lovable’s general case.

what_it_does: The preview toolbar includes a device toggle for mobile view. Generated projects are standard responsive web applications rather than native mobile binaries.
how_it_works: Preview renders the same app at a mobile viewport for inspection.
scoped_clone_reason: Responsive dashboard preview matters, but native mobile distribution does not.

what_it_does: Users can select elements in the live preview and directly adjust text, colors, sizing, spacing, and images without spending an AI regeneration. The toolbar is Lovable’s current visual-editing surface.
how_it_works: Stable JSX IDs, a client-side AST, Tailwind generation, and hot module replacement map preview edits to source.
scoped_clone_reason: The teardown calls DOM-to-source mapping skippable v1; chat captures most value.

what_it_does: Users can inspect a preview, review diffs, and decide whether to keep or revert generated changes. Collaboration drafts let a change remain separate until accepted.
how_it_works: Review occurs through preview, Changes/Timeline, and draft acceptance controls.
scoped_clone_reason: A human review gate is necessary before publishing generated actions.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud provisions a managed backend database for an app. Users can request data-backed features without manually configuring a separate backend dashboard.
how_it_works: Cloud is configured from the Lovable project through prompts.
scoped_clone_reason: Platform-owned schema makes generalized Cloud provisioning unnecessary.

what_it_does: Lovable can apply database changes as part of backend evolution. Version revert does not reverse database data or migrations, so schema changes require separate care.
how_it_works: Cloud migrations are applied through generated backend changes; history restores code only.
scoped_clone_reason: Platform owns and controls Action Model migrations; clone should not expose arbitrary migration generation.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud provides backend capabilities including file storage for applications. Generated apps can use storage alongside authentication and database features.
how_it_works: Cloud-managed storage is configured through the project backend.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model’s platform storage is already owned by the platform.

what_it_does: Lovable generates application data reads and writes against its managed backend. It can build CRUD-style application behavior from natural-language requests.
how_it_works: Generated frontend/backend code calls the project’s Cloud/Supabase services.
scoped_clone_reason: CRUD against a fixed Action Model schema is in scope even though general backend generation is not.

what_it_does: Lovable supports connecting projects to external Supabase and moving frontend hosting separately from the backend. External backends have feature-parity limitations.
how_it_works: Git/export and Supabase integration separate frontend code ownership from backend hosting.
scoped_clone_reason: The platform owns the database; external database portability is intentionally out of scope.

what_it_does: Lovable advises exporting data before removing Cloud and supports downloading the project codebase. Backend portability is primarily through managed or self-hosted Supabase.
how_it_works: Project settings and external deployment paths provide export/download operations.
scoped_clone_reason: Export protects client ownership but is not the core build loop.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud includes sign-up/login and built-in authentication for generated apps. Documented auth providers include email, phone, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and SAML SSO on relevant plans.
how_it_works: Cloud auth is configured through project prompts and managed backend services.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model owns identity and session authority; generated app auth is not needed.

what_it_does: Lovable-generated apps can implement role-aware access, and workspace/project roles govern who may view, edit, publish, or administer projects.
how_it_works: Permissions are enforced at workspace/project levels and app-level roles are generated in Cloud apps.
scoped_clone_reason: Tenant/project permissions remain necessary even with a fixed backend.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud advertises row-level security so users see only data intended for them. The teardown flags LLM-authored RLS as a known general-purpose risk.
how_it_works: RLS policies are attached to managed database tables and generated as part of Cloud backend work.
scoped_clone_reason: Platform-owned schema and policies remove the generalized LLM-RLS problem.

what_it_does: Lovable provides secrets management for runtime integrations and backend services. Credentials are kept out of generated source and used by managed functions/connectors.
how_it_works: Secrets are configured in the project and injected into backend execution.
scoped_clone_reason: Platform connectors and credentials are owned centrally rather than exposed to generated tenants.

what_it_does: Lovable can ask up to four clarifying questions with options or free text before proceeding. Plan approval is an explicit handoff from planning to execution.
how_it_works: Answers are stored in the browser for the request, and approving a plan switches to Build mode.
scoped_clone_reason: Approval is useful, but Action Model can use simpler structured input.

what_it_does: Lovable AI adds runtime AI features to generated apps without requiring users to create provider API keys or manage multiple billing relationships. Documented use cases include chat, summarization, classification, document Q&A, translation, workflows, and image generation.
how_it_works: Lovable routes app AI requests through its managed AI gateway and normalizes provider plumbing. Docs state the connector 'currently offers models from Google and OpenAI'; Gemini models are the documented default (Gemini 3.7 Flash), and the launch blog named Google Gemini only. [AUDIT 2026-08-27: was 'Google Gemini-powered layer' — docs.lovable.dev/features/ai lists OpenAI models too.]
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model already owns the model gateway and runtime; duplicating Lovable AI adds no scoped value.

what_it_does: Lovable’s integration surface supports connecting apps to external services and APIs, including webhook-style workflows. The public integration docs describe app connectors and API integration paths.
how_it_works: Generated backend functions or connector actions call external services with managed credentials.
scoped_clone_reason: The platform owns the relevant data and integrations for this client. what_it_does: Lovable supports chat connectors through MCP, custom MCP servers, and publishing a generated app as an MCP server. MCP lets Lovable pull context or invoke tools exposed by connected systems.
how_it_works: MCP servers are configured as connector endpoints and surfaced through the chat reference/action picker.
scoped_clone_reason: MCP is useful for future ecosystem reach but not required for the constrained builder.

what_it_does: Teams can create a custom connector for an API that is not in Lovable’s catalog. Connector knowledge can be made available to the agent and project.
how_it_works: Custom connector setup supplies endpoint/auth/schema context to the connector layer.
scoped_clone_reason: No connector fleet is required when the platform owns the database and app services. how_it_works: API details and credentials are supplied to generated backend calls or custom connectors.
scoped_clone_reason: General API breadth is a Lovable complexity that the fixed Action Model surface deletes. what_it_does: Plan mode investigates a request without modifying code and produces a structured implementation plan. Users can highlight and revise sections, inspect diffs, then approve the plan to begin Build mode.
how_it_works: Plans live in .lovable/plan.md, are archived on approval, and each Plan message costs one credit.
scoped_clone_reason: Planning is valuable for risky changes but not needed for every constrained action.

what_it_does: Build mode is Lovable’s autonomous execution mode for implementing features, fixes, refactors, and multi-file changes. It explores project context, edits files, and can inspect logs, network activity, and browser behavior.
how_it_works: The agent executes tools and surfaces activity, file diffs, and summaries in Details view.
scoped_clone_reason: Autonomous constrained execution is the primary builder capability.

what_it_does: Lovable runs multiple read-only subagents in parallel when a request has several independent parts. Docs name two types: generic subagents (findings in a specific shape — comparison, checklist, summary, review) and Explore (traceable evidence, uses the most capable model). Subagents cannot edit, create, or delete files; the main agent combines their findings. [AUDIT 2026-08-27: 'roles such as Researcher, Reviewer, and Synthesiser' was not in the source — those role names do not appear on docs.lovable.dev/features/subagents.]
how_it_works: Subagents are dispatched by the main agent for independent sub-questions and return findings for the main agent to synthesize; they are read-only.
scoped_clone_reason: Parallelism improves general Lovable throughput but the scoped app can use one constrained agent.

what_it_does: Workspace and project Knowledge store persistent instructions such as coding standards, schema, architecture, terminology, and design guidance. Lovable loads this context together with code, connectors, and repository instruction files.
how_it_works: Workspace knowledge is admin-owned; project knowledge is editable by project editors, with each field capped at 10,000 characters.
scoped_clone_reason: Fixed schema/design context is a core simplification and quality control for Action Model.

what_it_does: Build mode can inspect failures and offer a Try to fix action when a build error appears. Fix attempts are separately metered and can consume free-fix allowances or credits.
how_it_works: The agent reads diagnostics and reruns repair work as a follow-up request.
scoped_clone_reason: A bounded repair loop is useful, but broad self-improvement is not required.

what_it_does: Users can stop a running request, undo the latest edit, or wrap up when credits run out. Stopping preserves completed work and charges for work already performed.
how_it_works: The chat activity card exposes stop/undo; credit exhaustion pauses the request for Add credits or Wrap up.
scoped_clone_reason: Long-running generation needs explicit interruption and safe completion controls.

what_it_does: Lovable can inspect logs, network activity, and browser behavior to diagnose and verify changes. Most verification tools run when requested rather than automatically on every request.
how_it_works: The agent invokes browser/testing/diagnostic tools and reports results in the activity timeline.
scoped_clone_reason: Verification matters, but the initial scoped clone can use a small fixed smoke-test set.

what_it_does: Details view shows a Timeline of agent steps and tool calls plus a Changes view of file diffs. Activity cards summarize edits, commands, web searches, browser tests, and subagents.
how_it_works: The runtime emits structured activity events tied to the request.
scoped_clone_reason: Receipts make autonomous changes reviewable and debuggable.

what_it_does: Lovable supports reusable Skills invoked through slash commands to provide specialized instructions or workflows. Skills can be added from the chat action menu.
how_it_works: A slash command selects a stored skill definition that enriches the current request.
scoped_clone_reason: Curated workflows could follow later; fixed prompts are sufficient for v1.

what_it_does: Lovable provides an interactive preview of the generated app inside the editor. Preview runs alongside the agent and supports visual inspection before publishing.
how_it_works: The project is served in a managed development environment and rendered in the preview pane.
scoped_clone_reason: Sandbox preview iframe is in the teardown’s minimal 80%-value set.

what_it_does: Lovable can reproduce issues and test behavior through browser interactions. Browser checks are visible as activity and can be used to re-verify a fix.
how_it_works: Build mode invokes browser testing against the project preview.
scoped_clone_reason: A narrow smoke-test harness is useful, but broad browser automation is not necessary initially.

what_it_does: Lovable provides security views and integrates security scanning, with first-party documentation for Aikido and Wiz. Security scans identify issues in generated projects and can surface fix actions.
how_it_works: Scans run against project code/configuration and findings are shown in security views; security scans do not count as normal chat usage per chat docs.
scoped_clone_reason: The teardown says the platform-owned schema removes the main LLM-RLS risk; a full Wiz/Aikido program is outside scope.

what_it_does: Lovable puts generated changes behind previews, diffs, approvals, and collaboration draft acceptance. Users decide when a draft or plan should enter the main project.
how_it_works: Review controls operate at plan, draft, version, and publish boundaries.
scoped_clone_reason: Human acceptance before live publication is required for client-facing automation.

what_it_does: Lovable hosts published apps with managed production hosting, automatic deployments, SSL, global delivery, backend, databases, and infrastructure. Apps can be published directly from chat with publish/deploy/ship language.
how_it_works: Publishing promotes the project to Lovable-managed hosting; hosting and runtime features consume run credits.
scoped_clone_reason: Auto-hosting and a managed deploy target are explicitly in scope and are commodity with wildcard DNS plus build upload.

what_it_does: Paid plans can connect a custom domain to a project. Lovable verifies DNS, issues certificates automatically, and supports one primary domain with redirects from other domains.
how_it_works: Manual DNS uses an A record/TXT verification flow; certificates are provisioned automatically and TLS 1.2+ is enforced.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful for client launch, but subdomain publishing is enough for the first scoped release.

what_it_does: Every published project retains a lovable.app URL and can be published to a generated subdomain. Chat commands can request a subdomain during publishing.
how_it_works: Publishing assigns an [url-subdomain].lovable.app address that the platform routes to the project's hosted build; Business/Enterprise workspaces may use app-name.workspace-subdomain.lovable.app. [AUDIT 2026-08-27: 'Wildcard platform DNS' was INFERRED — docs.lovable.dev/features/custom-domain documents an A record to edge IP 185.158.133.1 for custom domains and states no wildcard mechanism for lovable.app subdomains.]
scoped_clone_reason: Subdomain deploys are explicitly called commodity in the teardown and belong in the minimal set.

what_it_does: Lovable projects can be deployed outside Lovable to platforms such as AWS, GCP, Azure, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or self-managed infrastructure. Git sync/download provides the handoff.
how_it_works: The output is a standard Vite + React project; operations, SSL, scaling, and monitoring shift to the operator.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model owns the deploy target; external hosting adds portability work without client value.

what_it_does: The generated frontend can run in Docker, Kubernetes, VMs, or other Node/static hosting environments. Lovable’s editor and agent themselves cannot be self-hosted in a customer VPC.
how_it_works: Download/Git export supplies the app; the managed builder remains external.
scoped_clone_reason: Self-hosting the generated app is not needed under platform-owned hosting.

what_it_does: Lovable documents a mobile app for building, prompting, and reviewing projects from a phone or tablet. This is a companion client, not native app distribution for generated projects.
how_it_works: The mobile client accesses the same managed Lovable projects and editor workflows.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model needs responsive client access, not a separate mobile companion app.

what_it_does: Lovable owns and operates the hosted application runtime, managed backend, infrastructure, secrets, and AI provider access for hosted projects. Users can export the frontend but not self-host the Lovable builder platform.
how_it_works: Managed hosting abstracts infrastructure operations and exposes project-level deployment controls.
scoped_clone_reason: The scoped clone should own one simple runtime target rather than general portability.

what_it_does: Lovable hosting advertises automatic deployments and environment management alongside preview environments. Published versions are marked and can be rolled back through history.
how_it_works: Project changes flow from preview/build to the hosted deployment path.
scoped_clone_reason: A single environment is sufficient initially; promotion complexity is deleted by scope.

what_it_does: Lovable documents SEO and AI-search optimization features and guidance, including integrations such as Google Search Console. The teardown identifies deep SEO/SSR, including TanStack Start, as irrelevant to dashboard scope.
how_it_works: SEO metadata and framework/server-rendering changes are generated in the app code and connected services.
scoped_clone_reason: Dashboard clients do not need Lovable’s marketing-site SEO/SSR surface.

what_it_does: Users can download a project codebase from Project settings or the code editor. Downloaded code can be opened locally and deployed outside Lovable.
how_it_works: A zip/codebase download supplies the generated source without requiring GitHub.
scoped_clone_reason: Source ownership is desirable but not needed to prove the core builder loop.

what_it_does: Lovable’s documented backend portability path is managed Supabase or self-hosted Supabase, with feature-parity gaps. Removing Lovable Cloud deletes managed database, storage, auth, and functions, so data export is advised first.
how_it_works: Backend migration requires exporting data and rebuilding unsupported infrastructure when leaving Cloud.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model owns the backend and does not need generalized backend exit machinery.

what_it_does: Lovable can export and two-way sync project code with GitHub or GitLab, including branch switching and pull request creation. It cannot start a project from existing GitHub code.
how_it_works: A workspace connection authorizes the provider and a project repository link syncs one active branch at a time.
scoped_clone_reason: Git-backed versions are in the teardown’s minimal set, though the scoped clone can simplify to one repository.

what_it_does: Lovable automatically records versions for edits, supports bookmarks and previews, and can revert a project to an earlier version. Revert is all-or-nothing at the version level.
how_it_works: History rows link to messages and diffs; reverting restores project code and redeploys matching edge functions.
scoped_clone_reason: Git commit per generation is explicitly in the minimal scoped clone.

what_it_does: Lovable version revert restores code only; database records and migrations remain unchanged. Projects remixed from Cloud-backed projects may also lose access to pre-remix restores.
how_it_works: History intentionally separates source restoration from backend data state.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model controls schema/data migration policy and can provide a simpler atomic app version model.

what_it_does: History identifies the currently live version and permits restoring an earlier code version, which redeploys the app. Very old versions may remain viewable but not restorable.
how_it_works: Revert is confirmed in the History panel and then redeploys the restored code.
scoped_clone_reason: Safe rollback is required for a hosted generated app.

what_it_does: Remix creates an independent copy of a project snapshot while preserving the original. Optional project history and custom knowledge can be copied, but secrets, data, domains, collaborators, connectors, and version history are not.
how_it_works: The remix dialog selects a target workspace/region and produces an unpublished independent project.
scoped_clone_reason: Forking is useful for experimentation but not needed for the first client workflow.

what_it_does: Lovable preserves project chat history and lets users navigate from versions back to the originating message. Plans remain retrievable through chat history.
how_it_works: Messages are stored as project conversation context and linked to activity/version records.
scoped_clone_reason: Prompt-to-change traceability is important for generated client work.

what_it_does: Collaborators work in separate drafts with their own chat and preview, and changes merge only when the draft is accepted. Roles control who may edit, publish, administer, or transfer projects.
how_it_works: Draft acceptance creates a named edit group in history and role checks gate actions.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful for teams, but a single owner/reviewer path can ship first.

what_it_does: Lovable documents workspace audit logs as an enterprise/governance capability. The surface records administrative or workspace activity for oversight.
how_it_works: Audit events are exposed in workspace security/admin surfaces.
scoped_clone_reason: Enterprise audit logging is outside the scoped dashboard builder.

what_it_does: Workspaces group projects, members, billing, and settings, and project permissions constrain access. External collaborators can be granted project-specific access without a workspace seat.
how_it_works: Role-based workspace/project membership provides the tenancy model.
scoped_clone_reason: Multi-client isolation is required, though Action Model can use fewer roles.

what_it_does: Lovable separates projects and workspaces while allowing controlled cross-project read-only references. Connections with limited access restrict which collaborators can use a project.
how_it_works: Workspace permissions and connector access checks gate context and actions.
scoped_clone_reason: The platform must prevent one client’s generated app/context from crossing tenant boundaries.

what_it_does: Lovable stores secrets and connector credentials separately from project source. Remix copies receive fresh API keys and external services must be reconnected.
how_it_works: Managed secrets/connector stores inject credentials at runtime and keep them out of copied code.
scoped_clone_reason: The platform owns credentials and integrations, so generated tenant apps do not need this general connector isolation layer. [AUDIT-FOLLOWUP 2026-08-27 main session: verdict was deleted_by_scope citing the 'platform owns the DB' premise retracted in lovable-teardown-2026-08-26.md CORRECTION 27 Aug (platform owning its own Postgres says nothing about client dashboards wanting Gmail/Slack/Stripe; connectors importable via activepieces MIT, 728 connectors). Flipped to nice_to_have = real work, deferred by phasing, not deleted by scope.]

what_it_does: Lovable runs project development previews in isolated cloud environments and operates a large sandbox fleet. The teardown reports that Lovable abandoned its own fleet and bought Modal for scale.
how_it_works: Each preview environment contains an isolated project runtime; the exact current provider/architecture is partly undocumented in public docs.
scoped_clone_reason: A rented sandbox is required, but the teardown says to rent E2B/Modal/Daytona rather than build a fleet.

what_it_does: Cloud-backed remixes expose a region choice, and the selected Cloud region is locked once chosen. Enterprise GitHub options also document data-residency variants.
how_it_works: Region is selected during Cloud setup/remix and is not freely migrated afterward.
scoped_clone_reason: Multi-region residency is a general Lovable concern deleted by a single-platform deployment target.

what_it_does: Workspace admins/owners manage collaborators, roles, credit limits, SSO, integrations, and publishing/privacy settings on eligible plans.
how_it_works: Admin settings expose role, usage, security, and publishing policy controls.
scoped_clone_reason: Basic owner/editor permissions are needed; enterprise governance is not.

what_it_does: Lovable sells workspace subscription plans with plan-specific permissions and usage allowances. Paid plans unlock features such as custom domains and code access, while Business/Enterprise add governance.
how_it_works: Plan tier gates features and workspace roles; pricing is documented separately from per-use credits.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model can use a simple client/seat commercial model rather than reproducing Lovable tiers.

what_it_does: Credits meter Build/Plan activity and, for Cloud-hosted apps, runtime/AI usage. Plan messages cost one credit; Build charges vary with files, complexity, exploration, and tool usage.
how_it_works: A workspace credit balance is debited by build, plan, hosting/run, and AI work, with collaborators sharing the owner workspace balance.
scoped_clone_reason: The teardown recommends flat per-seat or no metering; unified build/run credits are a Lovable pain point, not a must-have.

what_it_does: Lovable shows actual credits used in activity details and More options, but does not provide an upfront Build estimate. Credit check-ins can pause work when a threshold is reached.
how_it_works: Usage is reported after/during work; default check-in threshold is documented as beta.
scoped_clone_reason: A simple usage receipt helps, but reproducing opaque credit economics is unnecessary.

what_it_does: Workspace owners/admins can set a default monthly credit limit and per-member overrides. Collaborators consume credits from the project owner’s workspace balance.
how_it_works: Limits are managed in workspace admin/billing settings.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful governance for teams, but flat client billing can avoid this complexity.

what_it_does: Lovable documents project logs and project usage/cost views for hosted apps. Build mode can also inspect logs and network activity while diagnosing a task.
how_it_works: Runtime and build diagnostics are surfaced in project/logging panels and agent activity.
scoped_clone_reason: Basic logs are useful; broad hosted observability is not required in v1.

what_it_does: Build errors surface Try to fix actions, and the agent can inspect logs, network activity, and browser behavior. Errors can be repaired through a follow-up request.
how_it_works: Diagnostics feed agent tool calls and activity receipts.
scoped_clone_reason: Generated code needs a bounded error-and-repair loop.

what_it_does: Lovable manages hosting, deployments, SSL, backend infrastructure, and scaling for hosted apps. External deployment transfers CI/CD, scaling, backups, monitoring, and compliance work to the operator.
how_it_works: Managed service abstracts those operational responsibilities behind project settings.
scoped_clone_reason: Owning one managed runtime is the scoped clone’s main complexity reduction.

what_it_does: Lovable publishes a filterable hub of community production-ready website and app templates (204 results at time of check). Filters observed: category (All/Websites/Apps), 20 subcategories, and 14 persona filters. Each card links to a template detail page. [AUDIT 2026-08-27: 'searchable' softened to 'filterable' — discovery is via filter links, no text search box observed; 'remixable' detail pages not confirmed on lovable.dev/templates itself.]
how_it_works: The catalog is a filtered web index; selecting a template starts a project/remix flow.
scoped_clone_reason: Templates accelerate onboarding but are not required for the constrained Action Model app shape.

what_it_does: Lovable’s public product materials document hosted projects, exports, and branded URLs, but no public white-label/OEM/API offering was found in the reviewed first-party sources. This row records the boundary as not sourced rather than asserting a legal absence.
how_it_works: undocumented
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model is building its own product surface, not reselling Lovable under another brand.

what_it_does: Lovable projects can be previewed and published to hosted URLs, and the teardown mentions an MCP preview rather than a white-label embed product. Public docs reviewed here do not define a general iframe/OEM embed contract.
how_it_works: Hosted URL and preview are documented; general embed terms are undocumented.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model needs its own preview iframe; Lovable’s commercial embed semantics are not needed.

what_it_does: Lovable exports standard project source that can be run and deployed outside the platform. Backend-dependent features may require rebuilding Supabase equivalents when leaving Cloud.
how_it_works: Source download/Git sync preserve frontend code while managed backend portability is partial.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful ownership property, but fixed platform runtime is sufficient for initial scope.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud is Lovable’s built-in backend for hosted apps, providing managed database, authentication, storage, and functions. Lovable’s deployment guidance identifies managed Supabase and self-hosted Supabase as the backend portability paths, while noting feature-parity gaps outside Cloud.
how_it_works: Cloud resources are provisioned and configured from the Lovable project through prompts; exact current provider implementation is only partly described in first-party docs.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model already owns the database, auth, storage, and function runtime; reproducing Lovable Cloud would duplicate the platform and reintroduce generalized backend provisioning.

what_it_does: The Chat panel is the primary conversational interface for asking Lovable to build, debug, explain, plan, or publish a project. The same conversation carries across Build and Plan modes, and the composer supports attachments, references, connectors, screenshots, and skills.
how_it_works: Users type or dictate a message in the prompt box, choose a mode, and submit; the request is recorded in project chat history and routed to the corresponding agent workflow.
scoped_clone_reason: Conversational input is the minimum interface for the scoped constrained builder and is explicitly in the teardown’s 80%-value set.

what_it_does: Cloud projects include managed file storage for application uploads and media. Storage is one of the backend capabilities that must be recreated when leaving Lovable Cloud.
how_it_works: Prompt-configured Cloud storage is accessed by generated app code and backend services.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model already owns platform storage; a general generated-app storage layer is unnecessary.

what_it_does: Lovable Cloud documents Jobs for scheduled or background application work. Jobs extend generated apps beyond request/response CRUD.
how_it_works: The managed Cloud runtime schedules or executes configured jobs; exact scheduler implementation is undocumented.
scoped_clone_reason: Platform-owned workflows replace a general-purpose generated job scheduler.

what_it_does: Cloud projects can use edge functions for server-side application logic and integrations. Edge functions are redeployed when code is reverted through version history.
how_it_works: Functions execute in the managed backend runtime and can use project secrets.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model owns its backend execution path; generated edge-function portability is out of scope.

what_it_does: App connectors are configured once with a shared account and work in both contexts: in chat while you build, and in the published app while people use it. Docs name Slack, HubSpot, and Google Sheets. Per-user account connection is a separate feature (app user connectors). how_it_works: Connector configuration supplies OAuth/API access and service knowledge to generated app code.
scoped_clone_reason: A deployed client dashboard connecting to external services is real client value, not deleted by platform DB ownership. Deferrable past first scope but not out of scope, and importable from a permissive OSS connector fleet rather than built. what_it_does: Chat connectors give Lovable’s agent access to connected services as conversational context or tools. They are distinct from connectors embedded into the generated application.
how_it_works: MCP-based or service-specific connector entries are selected from the chat actions/@ reference surfaces.
scoped_clone_reason: Future ecosystem integrations may help, but the constrained first release can avoid external connector breadth.

what_it_does: App-user connectors allow end users of a generated application to connect their own accounts to supported services. This adds per-user OAuth and credential handling beyond project-level integrations.
how_it_works: User connection authorization is mediated by the connector layer and app runtime.
scoped_clone_reason: Per-user OAuth is genuinely deferrable for the first scope (a shared project-level account covers most dashboard cases), but it is deferred by phasing, not deleted by the platform owning the DB — end users connecting their OWN Gmail/Slack is orthogonal to who owns Actionist's Postgres. what_it_does: Lovable documents Stripe integration and in-app payments, with Paddle also listed among connector additions. Generated projects can wire billing/payment flows through those services.
how_it_works: Payment integration is configured through connector/API setup and generated application code.
scoped_clone_reason: Client billing is handled by Action Model’s platform, not generated per-app payments. what_it_does: Lovable documents analytics for projects and deployed apps. Analytics provide usage or product measurement beyond build-time activity.
how_it_works: Analytics configuration is attached to the project/app runtime; implementation details vary by integration.
scoped_clone_reason: Useful later for builder telemetry, but not needed to create and publish the scoped app.

what_it_does: Lovable documents sensitive-data scanning as a security capability for identifying exposed secrets or sensitive values. It complements project security views and external scanners.
how_it_works: Scanning examines project content/configuration and surfaces findings for review.
scoped_clone_reason: The scoped system can keep credentials platform-side and avoid exposing generated tenants to this broad scan surface.

what_it_does: The workspace security center centralizes security posture and controls for eligible workspaces. It is an administrative surface rather than an app-runtime feature.
how_it_works: Workspace admins inspect and manage security settings from the security center.
scoped_clone_reason: Enterprise workspace governance is outside the scoped product’s needs.

what_it_does: Business/Enterprise Lovable workspaces document SSO and SCIM for centralized identity and provisioning. These features govern workspace access rather than generated-app users.
how_it_works: SAML/SCIM administration is configured at workspace level and gated by plan/role.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model can defer enterprise identity provisioning while retaining basic project roles.

what_it_does: Lovable documents audit logs for workspace activity and governance. The feature supports oversight of administrative actions in higher-tier workspaces.
how_it_works: Events are recorded and surfaced through the audit-log admin page.
scoped_clone_reason: Not required for a single-platform scoped builder’s initial release.

what_it_does: Lovable provides design templates and guidance to accelerate consistent visual output. Templates package repeatable layout and styling patterns for common application types.
how_it_works: Template/design assets seed a new project and constrain generated visual choices.
scoped_clone_reason: Templates improve onboarding but the fixed Action Model schema/design system is the stronger constraint.

what_it_does: Lovable Build mode can generate or edit images and videos for projects, and Lovable AI documents Nano Banana image generation. Generated assets can be used in app visuals.
how_it_works: The agent invokes managed generation tooling and inserts resulting assets into project code/content.
scoped_clone_reason: Dashboard/product workflows do not require generative media creation in the scoped clone.

what_it_does: Lovable supports a Figma plugin, Figma MCP, and .fig upload as separate design-ingestion paths. All provide structured design context instead of requiring screenshot-only imitation.
how_it_works: The parser extracts variables, colors, typography, and frame structure before generation.
scoped_clone_reason: Design import is useful but not necessary when Action Model supplies its own design system.

what_it_does: Lovable’s Publish surface deploys a project, shows its live URL, and supports republishing after changes. Hosted apps retain the lovable.app address even when a custom domain is configured.
how_it_works: Publish promotes the current project to managed hosting and reports deployment state.
scoped_clone_reason: The scoped product needs an explicit publish gate and stable live URL.

what_it_does: Lovable documents branded workspace URLs as a workspace-level URL customization capability. This is separate from per-project custom domains.
how_it_works: Workspace admins configure the branded URL under workspace settings; detailed mechanics are plan-gated.
scoped_clone_reason: A branded workspace URL is commercial polish, not required for the core builder.

what_it_does: Lovable supports GitLab as an alternative code-sync destination. The GitLab path provides external source ownership alongside GitHub sync.
how_it_works: A project repository link synchronizes generated source with the connected GitLab repository.
scoped_clone_reason: Git-backed versions matter; GitLab provider breadth does not for the first scoped release.

what_it_does: Collaborators can work in separate drafts with their own chat and preview, and merge changes only after accepting a draft. Draft acceptance becomes a named edit group in history.
how_it_works: Each draft is an isolated project copy until accepted into the shared project.
scoped_clone_reason: A single owner/reviewer path can ship before full collaborative drafts.

what_it_does: Lovable can reference another project in the same workspace as read-only context. Access follows workspace permissions.
how_it_works: The context picker resolves project references and injects permitted content into the request.
scoped_clone_reason: Fixed schema/design context is enough initially; broad cross-project context can wait.

what_it_does: Lovable exposes an MCP server integration so external AI clients can work with Lovable projects. This is a product-to-agent integration, not just an app connector.
how_it_works: An MCP endpoint exposes supported Lovable project actions to connected clients.
scoped_clone_reason: Action Model does not need to expose Lovable’s own platform as an MCP server.

what_it_does: Lovable maintains first-party documentation and blog pages describing product features, constraints, and integrations. These pages are evidence of documented product claims, not independent verification of implementation quality.
how_it_works: Documentation is published on docs.lovable.dev and lovable.dev/blog.
scoped_clone_reason: Public signal metadata is not a runtime capability to clone.
